title: NY State Senate · District 14
area: Southeast Queens, including Jamaica, St. Albans, Springfield Gardens, Laurelton, Cambria Heights and Rosedale.

context.text: Incumbent Leroy Comrie is unopposed on the general-election ballot; the Democratic and Republican primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were both canceled and no Republican, Conservative or other-party candidate filed for the seat.

summary.text: Leroy Comrie is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Senate District 14 in southeast Queens. A lifelong South Queens resident and former community school board president, he served twelve years on the New York City Council before his 2014 election to the Senate, where he chairs the Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions. He is running unopposed in the general election.

background.text: Born in New York City to Ruby Frith-Comrie and Leroy Comrie Sr., immigrants from Jamaica; grew up in the South Queens communities he now represents.
Attended P.S. 116, I.S. 8 and Jamaica High School, then the University of Bridgeport, where his official biography says he developed his interest in politics and government.
Was elected president of his local community school board before becoming a public official.

Served twelve years on the New York City Council (2002 to 2013) representing a southeast Queens district, holding the positions of Deputy Majority Leader and Chairman of the Queens Delegation and chairing the Rules, Consumer Affairs, and Land Use committees.
His official biography lists among his Council accomplishments increasing senior tax exemptions, creating the city's first foreclosure prevention program, and curtailing payday loans.
Launched a campaign for Queens Borough President in 2013 but dropped out before the primary and endorsed Melinda Katz.

Elected to the New York State Senate in 2014, defeating incumbent Malcolm Smith and Munir Avery in the Democratic primary and running unchallenged in the general election; assumed office January 1, 2015.

Chairs the Senate Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions and is a member of the Budget and Revenue, Finance, Procurement and Contracts, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Rules committees and the Select Majority Task Force on Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises; was appointed to the Public Authorities Control Board in 2019.

Named a 2026 New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame Honoree; his official biography says he is a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic and Asian Legislative Caucus, a lifelong member of Saint Albans the Martyr Episcopal Church, and has been married to Marcia Moxam since 1990, with two adult children.

priorities.text: Says government must be responsive to the needs of all people, citing access to quality education, healthcare and services for seniors as priorities.
priorities.quote: government must be responsive to the needs of all people

priorities.text: Lists programs and resources for youth and avenues to enhance small business growth among his priorities.
Prioritizes increased public safety measures and smart, sustainable economic development that provides living-wage jobs in the community.

record.text: Chairs the Senate Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, which oversees the state's public authorities including the MTA and Port Authority; also serves as Democratic Whip and on the Budget and Revenue, Finance, Procurement and Contracts, Rules, and Racing, Gaming and Wagering committees.

Sponsored S10487, the "Data Center Water Stewardship and Reuse Act," which would require large-capacity data centers to use water recycling and closed-loop cooling systems; remained in the Senate Environmental Conservation Committee as of May 15, 2026.

Sponsored S10293, the "Deed Theft Eviction Protection Act," which would require courts to stay eviction warrants while a property owner's title is actively contested in court; remained in the Senate Housing, Construction and Community Development Committee as of May 11, 2026.

Sponsored S10222, which would restructure Port Authority of New York and New Jersey organization, public appearance and notice rules and establish a Port Authority transportation advisory committee; remained in the Senate Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee as of May 7, 2026.

Biographical details come from Comrie's official Senate biography, supplemented by Ballotpedia and Wikipedia for dates and the 2013 borough president campaign.
